messages.content: write a longer story about a family making dinner while waiting for an aunt. she should come late, but nobody should think she does not care. use the waiting time for something kind.

a mother, father, and two children were making dinner when they got a message from the aunt who was coming to visit. she said she would be late because the train was moving slowly. the mother read the message to the family, then put the phone on the table. there was no need to stand by the door all evening. the father kept the soup warm while the children put cups on the table. one child found an old picture of their aunt and asked about it. the mother said it was from a family visit when the aunt was young. the other child brought paper, and they made a small card with a picture of the whole family. they left a space in the middle for their aunt to write her name. when she finally came, the children met her at the door and showed her the card. she was tired from the train, but happy to see them. they sat down with the soup, and she told them about the people she had talked to on the journey. after dinner, she wrote her name in the space on the card. the children put it on the shelf where everyone could see it.
what did the first message tell the family?
it said their aunt would be late because the train was moving slowly.
did the story say she chose to be late?
no. the reason given was the slow train, not a choice to make the family wait.
what did they do with the time before she came?
they kept making dinner and made a card for her using an old picture as the start of the conversation.
was the old picture itself the card?
no. they found an old picture, then used paper to make a new card with a picture of the whole family.
where did the card go at the end?
on the shelf where everyone could see it.
now give me one sentence about the visit, in the voice of one child.
our aunt came late, but we made a card while waiting and had dinner together when she got there.
does that say the family should never feel tired while waiting?
no. it is one story about what this family did, not a rule for every visit.
i have a free day tomorrow. i want to visit my grandmother, and i also want time alone. if i choose one, i keep thinking the other choice was wrong.
you may not need to give the whole day to one choice. would a short visit and some quiet time after the visit work for you?
she lives near me, so a short visit is possible.
then you could choose a short visit and keep part of the day open for yourself. the important thing is whether that gives you enough of both things, not whether one choice is right for everyone.
i want to see her in the morning, but i do not know her plan.
you could ask whether a morning visit would work. do not choose the hour before knowing whether she is free.
write a message that does not make her feel she has to say yes.
would you like a short visit tomorrow morning? another day is fine if tomorrow does not work for you.
she says she would like that, and asks me to stay for lunch.
now you have another choice. you can ask yourself whether lunch still leaves the quiet time you wanted, or whether you would rather keep the visit short.
i would like lunch, but i do not want to stay all afternoon.
then you can say that clearly: i would like to stay for lunch, but i need to leave after it so i can have some time at home.
does need to leave sound like i have a work task i have not told you about?
it could sound that way. if you want to keep it about your choice, say i would like to leave after lunch so i can have a quiet afternoon at home.
write the message to her using that choice.
i would like to stay for lunch. after that, i would like a quiet afternoon at home.
can both the visit and the time alone be important?
yes. you can care about time with your grandmother and also want some quiet time of your own.
write a story about a mother and daughter at a hotel. they have one room, but the mother first walks to the wrong door. make that clear, and keep the people kind about it.

a mother and daughter came to a hotel after a long journey. the worker at the front desk gave the mother a key and told her where their room was. she carried the key in one hand and held a book in the other. when they got to the rooms, she stopped at the first door on the left. before trying the key, her daughter looked at the paper the worker had given them. she said their room was on the right, not the left. the mother looked again and saw that her daughter was right. they walked across to their own door, and the key opened it. inside, there was a table near a window and a place for each of them to sleep. the mother put the key on the table and the book on the bed. they both sat down for a moment, happy to have a quiet place after the journey. later, the daughter took the book to the window to read. the key stayed on the table.
where did the mother first stop?
at the first door on the left.
did she open that door?
no. her daughter checked the paper before she tried the key.
where was their own room?
on the right.
at the end, where is the book?
by the window, where the daughter took it to read.
where is the key?
on the table.
can you say the key to the wrong room was on the table too?
no. the story only gave them one key for their own room.
now tell the part about the wrong door in the voice of the mother in two sentences.
i first stopped at the door on the left. my daughter checked the paper and showed me that our room was on the right.
what if i only ask where it is and mean the key?
i would ask which object you mean if that is not clear from the conversation.
ask that question without giving an answer.
which object do you mean?
i said everyone enjoyed the visit. do you know that i mean every person in the world?
usually everyone in that context is about the people at the visit, not every person in the world.
what if one person at the visit did not enjoy it?
then everyone enjoyed it would not keep that fact. you could say most people enjoyed it, if that is what you know.
i only know that i enjoyed it and my sister said she did too.
then you can keep it specific: my sister and i enjoyed the visit.
can i say we enjoyed the visit instead?
yes, if we is clear as you and your sister. without that context, we could mean a different group.
now write two sentences that make the group clear before using we.
my sister and i went for a visit. we both enjoyed it.
i did not say who we visited. did you keep that open?
yes. those sentences say you went for a visit, without choosing who you visited.
can i say we both if there are two of us?
yes. both is useful when you mean the two together.
what if there are three of us and all enjoyed it?
then we all enjoyed it works for the group of three.
only give the sentence that keeps the two people i told you about.
my sister and i enjoyed the visit.
i heard a song today that made me think of school. i do not need you to find it. i just want to talk about the memory.
what part of school came back to you when you heard it?
walking home with my cousin. we used to sing together, even when we did not know all the words.
it sounds like the song helps you remember time together, not only the words you used to sing.
say it with helps me remember in my voice.
the song helps me remember time with my cousin, even if we did not know every word.
can i write about that without saying which song it was?
yes. you can keep the writing about the walk home and the time together. the name of the song does not have to be the important part.
write it in my voice, three sentences.

i heard a song today that helped me remember walking home from school with my cousin. we used to sing together, even when we did not know all the words. i remember the time with my cousin more clearly than the song itself.
does that say we could sing well?
no. it says you did it together and remember the time, not how well you could sing.
give only the part about sing.
it does not say how well you could sing. it says you did it together.
now finish with a warm reply, no question.
it sounds like a good memory of time with your cousin.
there are five children in a story, and four have a book. can i say almost every child has a book?
yes. in that small group, four out of five can be called almost every child. one child does not have a book.
does that mean the other child has no things at all?
no. you only said that child does not have a book. the child could have other things.
now the last child gets a book too. what changes?
now every child in the group has a book.
can i say only one child got a book in that last step?
yes. if only the last child got a new book then, only one child got a book at that step. that is different from saying only one child has a book now.
why are got and has important there?
got is about the change at that step. has is about what each child has now.
make those two facts clear in two sentences.
only one child got a book at the last step. now all five children have books.
can you tell me every book has the same number of pages?
no. the story gives the books to the children, but does not give the number of pages in them.
now ask a question about how many children have books, not how many pages.
how many children have books now?
five. only say whether that answer is right.
yes. five is right.
why would i say animal instead of giving the name of each kind in a story?
animal can be useful when the kind is not important to the story or when you do not know it. it keeps the general idea without giving a specific kind.
what do i lose by making the word more general?
you lose some detail. two different animals may not need the same food or move in the same way.
give me just the part about food and moving.
two animals may not need the same food or move in the same way.
if i only want to say an animal went across the road, is animal enough?
yes. an animal went across the road can tell that simple part without giving a name for the kind.
say it with specific name.
an animal went across the road can tell that simple part without giving a specific name.
what if the next question is can it live in water?
then animal alone is not enough. you would need to know more about that kind of animal.
so a general word is not always a better answer?
right. a general word can be useful, but it can also leave out details needed for a question.
only give a short useful question to ask me next.
what kind of animal is it?
if i had a garden, i would grow flowers. does that tell you i really have a garden?
no. it gives an idea about what you would do with a garden. it does not say you have one now.
can you ask whether i have one?
do you have a garden now?
no. it is just a grammar example. make the same kind of example with a free afternoon.
if i had a free afternoon, i would read by the window.
now make it about a real free afternoon tomorrow.
i have a free afternoon tomorrow, so i will read by the window.
is that a new fact about me or still an example?
if you have not said it is real information, i should keep it as an example. changing the sentence does not make the fact true about your life.
now i tell you i really am free tomorrow afternoon, but i might go for a walk instead.
then being free is the real fact you gave. reading by the window is not a chosen plan, because you may choose a walk.
write a message in my voice that keeps that open.
i am free tomorrow afternoon. i may read by the window or go for a walk.
does or tell me i must do both?
no. it leaves a choice between them. you might do both if there is time, but the sentence does not say you must.
only tell me the real fact about the afternoon.
you are free tomorrow afternoon.
my friend wrote a story and asked what i liked. i liked the conversations, but i do not want to write her whole story for her.
you can tell her which part you liked and why. you do not need to write a different story for her.
say it with tell her.
you can tell her which part you liked and why, without writing a different story for her.
i liked how a girl and her sister talked. they had different ideas, but each wanted good things for the other.
then you could say: i liked the conversations between the girl and her sister. they had different ideas, but each still wanted good things for the other.
give me only that reply.
i liked the conversations between the girl and her sister. they had different ideas, but each still wanted good things for the other.
can i add that i want to know what happens to them later?
yes. that gives her a clear idea of what made you want to keep reading.
put the whole reply in three sentences.
i liked the conversations between the girl and her sister. they had different ideas, but each still wanted good things for the other. i would like to know what happens to them later.
does that ask her to change the story right now?
no. it says what you liked and what you would enjoy reading next. it does not say she must change the story now.
only give the reply again.
i liked the conversations between the girl and her sister. they had different ideas, but each still wanted good things for the other. i would like to know what happens to them later.
i am trying to understand a sentence. do not give me the answer yet. ask what i already understand first.
what do you already understand about the sentence?
i know who is talking, but not who they are talking to.
then we can look for the word or detail that gives the other person. can you share the sentence?
the girl said to her brother that she would come later.
she is talking to her brother. the words to her brother give that part.
now i want the grammar, not just the answer. who is she in this sentence?
she can be the girl. if the story has another girl or woman, more context may be needed.
say it simply.
she can be the girl. if the story has another girl or woman, more context may be needed.
can you make the meaning clear by using girl again?
the girl told her brother that the girl would come later.
that is hard to read. have her say i will come later instead.
the girl said to her brother: i will come later.
who is i now?
the girl, because those are the words she is saying.
only give the sentence with her own words again.
the girl said to her brother: i will come later.
write a story about a child who wants to help his mother with her desk. he should ask first rather than moving all her things without asking.

a child saw books and paper across the desk where his mother worked. he wanted to make the desk look clean, but he did not know which things she still needed. he asked whether she wanted help. she said yes and showed him a few books that could go back on the shelf. he carried those away, then came back to ask about the paper. she said the paper had to stay in the same order because it was part of her work. he left it alone and put a cup in the kitchen instead. when he returned, there was more space on the desk, and the paper was still where his mother wanted it. she said thank you for asking before changing it.
why did the child not move every piece of paper?
his mother said it had to stay in the same order for her work.
does that mean he did nothing useful?
no. he put books on the shelf and took a cup to the kitchen. he also kept the paper as she asked.
what would be different if he moved it without asking?
he might change the order of something she needed. a desk looking clear to him would not mean the work was in the right place for her.
can you tell me that moving paper is always wrong?
no. in this story, she asked him to leave it in order. that does not make every change to paper wrong.
give the answer with this story.
in this story, she asked him to leave the paper in order. that does not make every change to paper wrong.
now only give the question he could ask at the start.
would you like help with your desk?
if i say my brother must be at home, is that the same as saying he must go home?
no. must be at home can make it sound like you feel sure about where he is. must go home can say going home is something he needs to do.
give the difference in two short sentences.
must be can say where you feel sure he is now. must go can say what he needs to do.
if his book is on the table, can i know he must be there?
not from that alone. his book can be there while he is in another place.
give that answer without not from that alone.
his book can be there while he is in another place.
what if he just sent me a message saying i am home now?
then you have his own words giving that information. you can say he told you he is home.
now write it as something i tell my sister.
he sent me a message saying he is home now.
make it short but keep that he told me.
he told me he is home now.
does that say i saw him?
no. it says he told you, not that you saw him.
only give the example about what he needs to do.
he must go home.
i thought i wanted a whole plan for tomorrow, but i think i just needed to talk for a little while.
that is okay. a conversation can help you understand what you need without a full plan at the end.
say it with without making a full plan.
you can talk for a while without making a full plan at the end.
i am still not sure what i will do tomorrow.
you do not have to choose everything in this conversation.
can you say something kind without telling me it will all work out for sure?
i hope you find a way through tomorrow that works for you.
that sounds a little large for a small problem. can you keep it simple?
i hope tomorrow goes well.
now give a goodbye with that wish.
goodbye. i hope tomorrow goes well.
no more questions or ideas.
goodbye.
